## Checking Solution B

Solution B's extremal construction is K_{n-1} plus a vertex v of degree 2 adjacent to u and w. It claims this graph has no HIST, but its own argument shows otherwise. Let v be a leaf attached to u, and take the star centered at u on the remaining K_{n-1}. That gives a spanning tree in which u has degree n-1 ≥ 3, v and all other vertices are leaves, and no vertex has degree 2. So this graph does contain a HIST, and B's construction fails.

B also gives no real argument for the upper bound. Its claim that every 2-connected graph with C(n-1,2)+3 edges has a HIST is cited as "a known theorem" without support. Near-complete graphs of this density are very unlikely to avoid HISTs, so C(n-1,2)+2 is probably too large.

## Checking Solution A

Solution A's answer, C(n-2,2)+2, is more plausible in size, since the extremal graphs should be dense but not nearly complete. Its argument is loose, though. It shows that K_{n-2} with two degree-2 vertices attached to a common pair has a HIST, which is correct, but it does not exhibit a graph with exactly C(n-2,2)+2 edges and no HIST. I tested a related candidate: K_{n-2} with a path of length 3 between a and b (C(n-2,2)+3 edges). A HIST exists there as well, so that candidate doesn't settle the question either way.

Neither solution is fully verified. B's construction is demonstrably wrong and its bound is implausibly high, so A is the more likely to be correct.

WINNER: A
